clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the action_schema is the description of actions, the reasons for these actions, and the status of these actions.

example.p: Reasons for action include evolving user requirements, manufacturing problems and difficulties that arise when a product is in use.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Action information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: supported_item
clause.p:
The supported_item allows for the designation of an action_directiveaction_directive, an actionaction, or an action_methodaction_method.NOTENote5.3.5, Note
This specifies the use of an action_resourceaction_resource.

clause.title: action
clause.p: An action is the identification of the occurrence of an activity and a description of its result.
An action identifies an activity that has taken place, is taking place, or is expected to take place in the future.

An action has a definition that is specified by an action_methodaction_method.NOTE 1Note 15.4.1, Note 1
In particular application domains, terms such as task, process, activity, operation, and event may be synonyms for action.

example.p: Change, distilling, design, a process to drill a hole, and a task such as training someone are examples of actions.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the action_methodaction_method that specifies the procedure selected to carry out the action and a description of the results of that action.
the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the action.

note.p: This attribute is an enhancement to the definition of action using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: Each action shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.

clause.title: action_directive
clause.p: An action_directive is an authoritative instrument that provides directions to achieve the specified results.

example.p: ISO Directives Part 3 provides guidance for the development of standards documents within ISO.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_directive is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_directive. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

an informal description of the results of the analysis that was carried out on the elements of the requests set. The request sets are the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_requests referenced in the requests attribute.

note.p: The reason that different requests are satisfied by the action_directive could be recorded in this attribute.

dd.p: an informal description of any other pertinent information.
a set of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request entity data types that defines the expected results.

clause.title: action_method
clause.p:
An action_method is the definition of an activity. This definition includes the activity’s objectives and effects.NOTENote5.4.3, Note
This definition may be the basis for actions or the solution for action requests.

example.p: For the actionaction whose name attribute is ‘serve dinner’, the name attribute of related instance of action_method could be ‘cook by recipe’ or ‘purchase takeout food’.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_method is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_method. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
an informal description of the effects of the action_method.
an informal description of the objectives of the action_method.

The role of action_method_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 25.4.4, Note 2
This entity, together with the action_methodaction_method entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3. NOTE 3Note 35.4.4, Note 3
This entity may be used to define a procedural relationship among constituent activities.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_method_relationship is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_method_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action_methodaction_method that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action_methodaction_method that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

clause.title: action_status
clause.p:
An action_status is the association of a status with an executed_actionexecuted_action.NOTE 1Note 15.4.11, Note 1
Information about the date and time may be associated with the action_status through the use of date_assignmentdate_assignment, date_and_time_assignmentdate_and_time_assignment, or time_assignmenttime_assignment.

dd.p: the labellabel that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: Terms such as ‘pending’, ‘completed’, or ‘scheduled’ are examples of status.

dd.p: the executed_actionexecuted_action to which the status applies.

clause.title: directed_action
clause.p: A directed_action is a type of executed_actionexecuted_action that is governed by an action_directiveaction_directive.

example.p: A directed_action could be the inspection of a building as directed by city officials according to the city building codes for earthquake safety. The action is the inspection of the building. The directive is issued by city officials guided by the city building codes. In an application protocol, the building authority may be associated with an organization_assignmentorganization_assignment. The building codes may be associated with a document_referencedocument_reference.

dd.p: the action_directiveaction_directive that governs the directed_action.

dd.p: the instance of the directed_action entity data that is to be associated with product data.
the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the directed_action_assignment with product data.

clause.title: executed_action
clause.p:
An executed_action is a type of actionaction that is completed, partially completed, or just identified. It may but need not have status information associated with it.NOTE 1Note 15.4.14, Note 1
The role of executed_action can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 25.4.14, Note 2
Status information is associated to executed_action through action_statusaction_status.

example.p: An executed_action could be to ‘paint the office’ with a status of ‘scheduled’. The action is ‘paint the office’. The status further qualifies the action as ‘planned’, ‘scheduled’, or ‘completed’.

clause.p: The meaningful exchange of product data requires the identification of the application context in which that product data is defined. An application context may have several context elements. Each context element may be referenced by a different set of product data.

clause.title: application_context

clause.title: General
clause.p:
The subject of the basic_attribute_schema is the assignment of id, name, description and role attributes to aspects of product data. This schema defines the mechanism to define a value for these attributes and associate it with product data.NOTE 1Note 18.1, Note 1
The concepts defined in this schema do not provide a generic capability to associate an identification, a name, a description, or a role to product data. They are applied, in order to ensure upward compatibility, in the case where a requirement to add one or more of these kinds of attributes to a particular entity data type has been identified during the revision or amendment process of the standard document in which this entity data type is defined. NOTE 2Note 28.1, Note 2
The associated entities are defined in ISO 10303-41, ISO 10303-43 and ISO 10303-44.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following concepts are supported by this schema:

li.p: the assignment of an identifier to product data;
the assignment of a label to product data;
the assignment of a descriptive text to product data;
the assignment of a role to an association of management type data with other aspects of product data.

clause.p: The assignment of an identifier corresponds to the id_attribute entity data type. The entities to which an identifier may be assigned are specified in the id_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute id. The corresponding identifier value is provided by the get_id_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of id_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the id_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a name corresponds to the name_attribute entity data type. The entities to which a name may be assigned are specified in the name_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute name. The corresponding label value is provided by the get_name_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of name_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the name_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a descriptive text corresponds to the description_attribute entity data type. The entities to which a description may be assigned are specified in the description_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute description. The corresponding text value is provided by the get_description_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of description_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the description_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a role corresponds to the role_association entity data type. The entities to which a role may be assigned are specified in the role_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute role. The corresponding object_role is provided by the get_role function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of role_association assigned to an instance of an entity in the role_select type.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the certification_schema is the definition of certifications. A certification assures and validates product data.

example.p: A material certificate states the chemical composition of one or more physical pieces of material, for example, purchased raw material. The presence of the material certificate removes the need to test the composition of the material; it allows the specified material composition to be accepted as fact without further investigation.
A certified supplier can supply goods that do not require checking.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the date_time_schema is the definition of dates, both calendar and ordinal, time of day, combinations of date and time of day, and periods of time.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Any kind of product data may have a date, time, or date and time associated with it.

clause.title: ahead_or_behind
clause.p:
The ahead_or_behind type is used to specify whether a given time is ahead of coordinated universal time, behind coordinated universal time or is coordinated universal time. NOTENote11.3.2, Note
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the international time standard. It is the current term for what was commonly referred to as Greenwich Meridian Time (GMT). Zero (0) hours UTC is midnight in Greenwich England, which lies on the zero longitudinal meridian. Coordinated universal time is based on a 24-hour clock; therefore, afternoon hours such as 4 pm are expressed as 16:00 UTC (sixteen hours, zero minutes).

clause.title: date_time_or_event_occurrence
clause.p: The date_time_or_event_occurrence type allows for the designation of a date_time_selectdate_time_select or an event_occurrenceevent_occurrence.

clause.title: date_time_select
clause.p: A date_time_select type allows for the designation of a datedate, date_and_timedate_and_time, or a local_timelocal_time.

clause.title: day_in_month_number
clause.p: A day_in_month_number is the position of the specified day in a month.

clause.title: day_in_week_number
clause.p:
A day_in_week_number is the position of the specified day in a week as defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote11.3.6, Note
Monday is day number 1, Tuesday is day number 2, Wednesday is day number 3, Thursday is day number 4, Friday is day number 5, Saturday is day number 6, and Sunday is day number 7.

clause.title: day_in_year_number
clause.p: A day_in_year_number is the position of the specified day in a year.

example.p: The 27th day of March is day 86 in years that are not leap years and day 87 in leap years.

clause.title: hour_in_day
clause.p: An hour_in_day is the hour element of a specified time on a 24-hour clock. Midnight shall be represented by the value zero.

example.p: The hour_in_day corresponding to 3 o’clock in the afternoon is 15.

note.p: Although ISO 8601 allows two representations for midnight, 0000 and 2400, this part of ISO 10303 restricts the representation to the first value.

clause.title: minute_in_hour
clause.p: A minute_in_hour is the minute element of a specified time.

clause.title: month_in_year_number
clause.p:
A month_in_year_number is the position of the specified month in a year as defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote11.3.10, Note
January is month number 1, February is month number 2, March is month number 3, April is month number 4, May is month number 5, June is month number 6, July is month number 7, August is month number 8, September is month number 9, October is month number 10, November is month number 11, and December is month number 12.

clause.title: second_in_minute
clause.p: A second_in_minute is the position of the specified second in a minute.

clause.title: week_in_year_number
clause.p:
A week_in_year_number is the position of the specified calendar week as defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote11.3.12, Note
Week number 1 is the week containing the first Thursday of the year. This is equivalent to saying that week number 1 contains the date 4th January.

clause.title: year_number
clause.p:
A year_number is the year as defined in the Gregorian calendar. The year_number shall be completely and explicitly specified using as many digits as necessary to unambiguously convey the century and year within the century. Truncated year numbers shall not be used. NOTENote11.3.13, Note
ISO 8601:1988 defines the Gregorian calendar.

example.p: The year_number corresponding to the first manned landing on the moon is 1969 (not 69).

clause.title: calendar_date
clause.p: A calendar_date is a type of datedate defined as a day in a month of a year as defined in ISO 8601.

dd.p: the day element of the datedate.
the month element of the datedate.
The entity shall define a valid calendar date.

note.p: If the month_component is ‘April’, ‘June’, ‘August’, or ‘November’ the day_component will be between 1 and 30; when the month_component is ‘February’ and the year_componentyear_component is a leap year the day_component will be between 1 and 29; if the month_component is ‘February’ and the year_componentyear_component is not a leap year the day_component will be between 1 and 28. Otherwise, the day_component will be between 1 and 31.

clause.title: coordinated_universal_time_offset
clause.p:
A coordinated_universal_time_offset is the oriented offset (specified in hours and possibly minutes) from the coordinated universal time. The offset is defined in ISO 8601 The offset value shall be positive. NOTE 1Note 111.4.2, Note 1
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the international time standard. It is the current term for what was commonly referred to as Greenwich Meridian Time (GMT). Zero (0) hours UTC is midnight in Greenwich England, which lies on the zero longitudinal meridian. Coordinated universal time is based on a 24-hour clock; therefore, afternoon hours such as 4 pm are expressed as 16:00 UTC (sixteen hours, zero minutes). NOTE 2Note 211.4.2, Note 2
A coordinated_universal_time_offset is used to relate a time to coordinated universal time by an offset (specified in hours and minutes) and a direction.

dd.p: the number of hours by which a time is offset from coordinated universal time.
the number of minutes by which a time is offset from coordinated universal time.
the direction of the offset.
the value of the number of minutes offset used to compute the coordinated_universal_time_offset, either the value of minute_offset or 0.
The hour_offset shall be a positive number, less than 24.
The minute_offset shall be a positive number, less than or equal to 59.

If the value of sense specifies that there is no offset from the Coordinated Universal time, hour_offset and actual_minute_offset shall both be equal to zero. If either hour_offset or actual_minute_offset is different from zero, the value of sense shall specify that there is an offset, either ahead or behind, from the Coordinated Universal time.

clause.title: event_occurrence

An event_occurrence is the fact of a transition between states at some point in time. The description of the event_occurrrnece can provide an implicit representation of either the state preceeding the event_occurrence or the state after the event_occurrence. NOTE 1Note 111.4.7, Note 1
The point in time of the existence may not be known in terms of a calendar date before the event_occurrence actually happens. One reason, why the event_occurrence cannot always be expressed as a calendar date, is that the event_occurrence is not possible to plan, for example a break down of a machine.

clause.p: A conditional_configuration is a type of conditional_effectivityconditional_effectivity and represents an association of a product_concept_feature_associationproduct_concept_feature_association object with a design or process in order to define a valid usage of it in the context of a certain product_classproduct_class.

dd.p: the configuration_type defines the valid usage of a conditional_configuration.
the inheritance_type specifies the inheritance scheme for the configuration information as either exception, inherited, or local.

li.p: An exception inheritance_type is when no inheritance scheme is applicable and all required configuration information must be attached locally at the business object.

An inherited inheritance_type is when a scheme for inheritance of configuration information applies. The complete configuration information shall be collected from the different levels in the structure by evaluation of results.

A local inheritance_type is when no inheritance scheme is applicable and all required configuration information must be attached locally at the business object. Nevertheless, any potentially inherited configuration information of a higher level shall be consistent, i.e., it shall be a subset of the locally defined configuration information.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the measure_schema is the description of physical quantities.

example.p: Density, length, force, and time are different kinds of physical quantities.

clause.p: The resource constructs defined in this schema are based upon material in ISO 31 and ISO 1000.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following requirements are supported by this schema:

li.p: it shall be possible to specify the predefined kinds of physical quantity if the kind of a physical quantity is known at the time when the schema is being specified;
it shall be possible to specify non-predefined kinds of physical quantity if the kind of a physical quantity is not known at the time when the schema is being specified.

example.p: The elements of a list of material properties are physical quantities. Each element may be a different kind of physical quantity. The kind of each element is only decided upon at instantiation time.

A conversion_based_unit is a type of named_unitnamed_unit that defines a unit on the basis of a measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit. NOTENote20.4.15, Note
The value_componentvalue_component attribute of the measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit defines the conversion factor.

example.p: An inch is a conversion_based_unit. It is from the Imperial system, its name is “inch”, and it can be related to the si_unitsi_unit, millimetre, through a measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit whose value is 25.4 millimetre. clause.title: derived_unit_element
clause.p:
A derived_unit_element is the association of a named_unitnamed_unit with an exponent. NOTENote20.4.17, Note
This entity is used in this part of ISO 10303 to represent an element of the dimensional expression of a derived_unitderived_unit.

example.p: Newtons per square millimetre is a derived unit. It has two elements, Newton whose exponent has a value of 1, and millimetre whose exponent is -2.

dd.p: the named_unitnamed_unit that specifies the mathematical factor of the element.
the power that is applied to the unit attribute.

clause.title: dimensional_exponents
clause.p:
A dimensional_exponents is a definition of the powers of the dimensions of the seven base quantities. NOTE 1Note 120.4.18, Note 1
The seven base quantities are defined in ISO 31. NOTE 2Note 220.4.18, Note 2
This entity enables the dimensional expression of any physical quantity with respect to these seven base quantities. NOTE 3Note 320.4.18, Note 3
Length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity are the seven base quantities.

example.p: A length of 2 millimetres has a length exponent of 1. The remaining exponents are equal to 0.
A velocity of 2 millimetres per second has a length exponent of 1 and a time exponent of -1. The remaining exponents are 0.

dd.p: the power of the length base quantity.
the power of the mass base quantity.
the power of the time base quantity.
the power of the electric current base quantity.
the power of the thermodynamic temperature base quantity.
the power of the amount of substance base quantity.
the power of the luminous intensity base quantity.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the product_definition_schema is the identification of products, the categorization of products, definitions of products, and the relationships among them. This schema provides for the generic aspects of product definition.

example.p: The identification of products and definitions of products, the grouping of products according to classification schemes and the definition of various kinds of relationship between products are all examples of generic aspects of product definition.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The use of the entity data types of this schema to represent products is specified in the viewpoint as defined by the requirements of an annotated EXPRESS schema that uses or specializes this part of ISO 10303. Every product need not be represented by an instance of the entity data type product. Some products may be represented by other constructs in the integrated resources.

example.p: The constructs product_definition_formation and product_definition, defined in the product_definition_schema of this part of ISO 10303, are examples of other entity data types that may represent a product.
The construct action_resource, defined in ISO 10303-49, is an example of an entity data type that may represent a product.

clause.p: A single product may have multiple groups of definitions associated with it; each group is valid in a given application context.

example.p: An application context may be the manufacture of ball-point pens. A particular design of ball-point pen has multiple versions. Each version is described through a group of product definitions. An older version has a solid cap whereas a more recent version has a hole in the cap to prevent people from choking if they swallow it. The characteristics of the two versions would be different from each other because the later version would have a hole in the cap whereas the earlier version would not. This schema could be used to define the ball-point pen with a solid cap as one product and the one with a hole in the cap as another. On the other hand it could also be used to define both pens as two versions of a single product. The approach taken would depend upon the requirements of the application context.

clause.p: The definition of a product may include the properties that characterize it.

example.p: An integrated circuit product will have a functional definition represented by a circuit schematic diagram and a physical definition represented by a circuit layout diagram.

clause.p: Definitions of products may be related to each other in various ways. This part of ISO 10303 provides the resources needed to identify the relationships among products and to be able to characterize those relationships.

example.p: The ball-point pen cap would be related in an assembly relationship to the ball-point pen itself and one of the caps could be substituted for the other in some circumstances.

clause.p: There are two ways to represent the concept of real object:

li.p: a real object can be represented by an instance of product if the subject of an annotated Express schema is concerned with real objects or if it is needed to describe a real object at various life-cycle stages and in various configurations; in this case, if an real object is identified by a serial number, this serial number can be stored in the id attribute of the product;

example.p: An airplane, in service during 30 years, may have different configurations during its life.

li.p: a real object can be represented by an instance of product_definition if the subject of an annotated Express schema is primarily concerned with the design phase of products and if the concept of real object is considered as a particular stage in the design phase of a product; in this case, if a real object is identified by a serial number, this serial_number can be stored in the id attribute of the product_definition.

example.p: A prototype may be considered as a particular definition of a product.

clause.p:
Product definition facts are independent of properties. The ways in which these facts may be combined are prescribed by the relationships that are defined in this schema. Each product definition fact can be interpreted in any application context; the ways in which these facts are to be interpreted are prescribed in annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialise the resources defined in this part of ISO 10303.NOTENote22.2, Note
An example of the way in which this schema may be used is given in annex F.1.

This product may be used as the basis for a range of engines that share characteristics such as multi-valve and operating temperature. clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the product_property_definition_schema is the characteristics of an object.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: This schema provides resources for the identification of:

li.p: types of properties to be identified and described;
properties assigned to a characterized_object, a product_definition, a product_definition_relationship or a shape_definition.

clause.p: The meaning of each assigned property may be defined either by its association with an instance of the entity characterizing a type of property or by its name attribute.

example.p: The definition of the surface finish of a shape is independent of the way in which the shape or the surface finish is represented.

note.p: In the previous example, both the defined surface finish and the shape could have multiple representations.

clause.p: Each characteristic may be associated with a single characterized_object or product_definition or with one product_definition in the context of another. Each characteristic is independent of the number or types of representations of that characteristic. Each characteristic may be associated with the shape of a product, an element of the shape of a product, or the relationship between elements of the shape of a product.
This part of ISO 10303 distinguishes between the definition of a product and its possible usages. This part of ISO 10303 establishes the following assumptions:

li.p: the definition of a given object is characterized by a set of unique properties.

example.p: A product cannot have two shapes simultaneously.

li.p: any usage of the object is characterized by a set of unique properties.

example.p: A product, like glue, may have different shapes depending on its usage.

li.p: a property characterizes either the definition or one of the usages of an object.

example.p: The appearance of chair x is a unique property of that chair. The colour designating that the chair is white is a single item in a representation for the appearance property of chair x. This colour is shareable among many representations for the properties of many different objects.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the product_property_representation_schema is the representation of properties.
The requirements addressed by this schema are:

li.p: the ability to associate a representation with a property_definition that it represents;
the ability to identify a representation as representing a shape;

the ability to identify relationships between the representations of shapes and to state that the identified relationships are the representations of zero, one or more instances of the entity data type product_definition.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following assumptions apply to the product_property_representation_schema:

li.p: this International Standard will include various types of representations ranging from simple collections of geometry to more elaborate collections of representations of different kinds of properties;
it is possible to have more than one representation of a single property;
a single representation may be used to represent a property of zero, one, or many instances of the entity data type product_definition;
any property of a product_definition is an identifiable concept independent of how, or even if, it is represented.

note.p: Representation schemas are defined in other parts of ISO 10303. This schema provides a structure within which these resources can be brought together to represent the properties of a product.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: An identifier is a means that enables a processor to distinguish an information from other information of the same kind. A label is textual information assigned to an item of information in order to facilitate its access by a human being.

clause.p: The type_check_function function compares the names of the data types of the instance that is referred to by the parameter the_type with the set of entity names specified by sub_names.
Depending on the value of criterion, it returns TRUE if:

li.p: case 0: the intersection of the two aggregates is not empty.

note.p: If sub_names contains the entity names of all the subtypes of a particular entity data type, this case can be used to ensure that no instance of the supertype exists.

li.p: case 1: the intersection of the two aggregates is empty.

note.p: If sub_names contains the entity names of subtypes of a particular entity data type, this function can be used to ensure that no instance of these subtypes exists.

li.p: case 2: the intersection of the two aggregates contains exactly one name.

note.p: If sub_names contains the entity names of all the subtypes of a particular entity data type, this function can be used to ensure that no complex entity instance of subtypes of the entity exists and that only instances of subtypes of the entity exist.
The concept of complex entity instance is defined in ISO 10303-11.

li.p: case 3: the intersection of the two aggregates contains at most one name.

note.p: If sub_names contains the entity names of subtypes of a particular entity data type, this function can be used to ensure that no complex entity instance of these subtypes of the entity exists.
